name: LIFE W3C threat-to-evidence coverage matrix
purpose: Map privacy and adjacent security threats to explicit observer capabilities, attack scenarios, evidence requirements, and claim ceilings. This is a coverage contract, not proof that a threat is implemented or mitigated.

sources.status: Group Note Draft dated 2026-09-27; evolving non-normative threat model
IETF Standards Track; SD-JWT selective disclosure, privacy considerations and unlinkability limits
W3C Data Integrity BBS Cryptosuites publication history and current status must be pinned per run
OpenID Foundation conformance suites for OpenID4VP/OpenID4VCI with HAIP; separate from privacy evaluation

status_vocabulary.mapped_existing_scenario: An existing scenario is relevant; runnable evidence and implementation coverage still require exact-head verification.
status_vocabulary.proposed_extension: A useful attack/evidence profile is specified but must not be called implemented until the profile and receipt exist.
status_vocabulary.separate_gate_not_linkability: Evaluate in a separate security, task-utility, or protocol-conformance lane; do not encode it as a linkability score.
status_vocabulary.external_telemetry: Requires an explicitly instrumented, consented and privacy-reviewed deployment trace; synthetic payloads alone cannot qualify it.

principles: The threat model is a catalogue of risks, not a claim that all risks are in scope for one metric.
A coverage mapping is not an implementation result; every release claim binds to an exact commit, data digest, observer profile, attack version, configuration and report digest.
Attacker-visible features and auxiliary-data budgets must be declared before scoring; labels, subject identities and split metadata stay in the evaluator trust domain.
Train, validation and test subjects and opaque pair handles must be disjoint; split identities before pair generation.
Report each attacker independently and the strongest observed attacker; never average away a successful linkage channel.
No universal credential-format winner or universal unlinkability score is defensible without a fixed task, observer capability, deployment boundary and cohort.
A lower linkability score is not a pass unless the compared presentations preserve task correctness, security policy and required conformance.
Inapplicable channels are N/A with a reason, never a privacy win.

attack_profiles.capability: Opaque pair handle only; no deliberate identity signal
attack_profiles.purpose: Detect label, row-order, pair-ID, split, or fixture-generation leakage
attack_profiles.expected_behavior: Chance-consistent discrimination within a preregistered tolerance and uncertainty interval

attack_profiles.capability: Deterministic equality and set-join rules over explicitly allowlisted artifacts
attack_profiles.purpose: Establish simple, interpretable attack baselines before learned models
attack_profiles.fit_data: No test fitting; any thresholds/joins are preregistered or trained on training identities
attack_profiles.expected_behavior: Known-answer positive and negative controls behave as specified

attack_profiles.capability: Regularized supervised attacker over observable feature vectors
attack_profiles.purpose: Measure whether combined weak signals outperform any single channel
attack_profiles.fit_data: Training/tuning identities only; transforms and hyperparameters frozen before test
attack_profiles.expected_behavior: Held-out subject evaluation, baseline comparison, feature ablations and subject-clustered uncertainty

attack_profiles.capability: Cross-session order, cadence and repeated-artifact history
attack_profiles.purpose: Detect linkage that requires multiple interactions
attack_profiles.fit_data: Entire subjects and their traces are partitioned before feature construction
attack_profiles.expected_behavior: Held-out identities and separate session-history / content-only ablations

attack_profiles.capability: Declared join of issuer, verifier, status service or multiple verifier logs
attack_profiles.purpose: Measure residual linkage under explicit collusion assumptions
attack_profiles.fit_data: Any linkage key available only to a party must remain scoped to that party's declared view
attack_profiles.expected_behavior: Report exactly which records are shared and which party learns the match

attack_profiles.capability: Consented deployment traces such as timings, network prefix, user-agent class and payload size
attack_profiles.purpose: Measure transport and device side channels not represented in credential bytes
attack_profiles.fit_data: Deployment-level train/test partition by subject and collection window
attack_profiles.expected_behavior: Separate timing-only, size-only, network-only and joint attacks

threats.name: Signature-based correlation
minimum_channels: message count and disclosed indexes where available
threats.evidence_floor: Compare repeated artifact against fresh derived presentations while matching claims, task and presentation schedule.
threats.claim_ceiling: Different proof bytes alone do not prove unlinkability; claims, disclosed structure, issuer keys and metadata can still link.

threats.name: Correlation via status and revocation lookup
threats.evidence_floor: Compare content-only, lookup-only and joined views; record status freshness and revocation latency.
threats.claim_ceiling: A privacy score without lookup traces does not cover status-channel correlation.

threats.name: Presentation exchange attacks
threats.evidence_floor: Pinned protocol conformance and negative replay/spoofing tests.
threats.claim_ceiling: Do not convert replay resistance or verifier acceptance into a linkability metric.

threats.name: Inappropriate or out-of-context credential use
threats.evidence_floor: Policy and authorization tests with expected accept/reject outcomes.
threats.claim_ceiling: A credential can be unlinkable yet be disclosed or accepted for the wrong purpose.

threats.name: Identifier-based correlation
threats.evidence_floor: Ablate each identifier and combination; report top-k retrieval and held-out re-identification by stratum.
threats.claim_ceiling: Selective disclosure of fields does not imply that the revealed combination is non-identifying.

threats.name: Untrustworthy holder/user-agent software
threats.evidence_floor: Wallet security review, permissions tests and consent-to-output checks.
threats.claim_ceiling: Artifact-level evaluation cannot establish trusted user-agent behavior.

threats.name: Excessive data disclosure
threats.evidence_floor: Measure unauthorized claims and task-completion rate alongside re-identification attack results.
threats.claim_ceiling: Lower linkage is not an improvement if the task fails or necessary claims are withheld.

threats.name: Metadata-based correlation
threats.evidence_floor: Compare metadata-only, claims-only and joint attacks; report smallest effective cohort and worst stratum.
threats.claim_ceiling: Cryptographic proof unlinkability does not remove metadata or profile-fingerprinting channels.

threats.name: Bearer credential reuse and correlation
threats.evidence_floor: Compare single-use and reused-artifact conditions under the same task.
threats.claim_ceiling: Absence of a subject ID is not evidence of non-correlation.

threats.name: Correlation via patterns of use
threats.evidence_floor: Evaluate complete held-out traces; keep each identity's full longitudinal history in one partition.
threats.claim_ceiling: Independent pair rows are not a substitute for a multi-session attacker.

threats.name: Disclosure to a malicious or deceptive verifier
threats.evidence_floor: Measure task-minimal disclosure, unauthorized claims, and linkage after aggregation across requests.
threats.claim_ceiling: Verifier-request and consent safety require separate policy tests; pair classification alone is insufficient.

threats.name: Issuer-side correlation and privacy subversion
threats.evidence_floor: Write down exactly what the issuer can observe before and after presentation; run a joined-log attack where supported.
threats.claim_ceiling: Unlinkable derived proofs cannot establish issuer-verifier unlinkability if issuance or operational events remain correlatable.

threats.name: Device tracking and fingerprinting
threats.evidence_floor: Use privacy-reviewed, consented traces and explicit retention rules; report channel ablations.
threats.claim_ceiling: Synthetic credential artifacts cannot qualify real network or device fingerprint resistance.

threats.name: Credential and data aggregation
threats.evidence_floor: Publish synthetic or lawful privacy-reviewed auxiliary-data provenance, coverage and join budget; evaluate with/without auxiliary data.
threats.claim_ceiling: No claim about real-world re-identification can be made from toy data alone.

threats.name: Unauthorized post-presentation use of data
threats.evidence_floor: Access-control, retention and deletion audits; provenance of actual downstream data use.
threats.claim_ceiling: Unlinkability does not prevent downstream misuse after information has been disclosed.

explicit_noncoverage.reason: Credential tampering, identity proofing, injection, key management, external resource integrity, honeypots, validity, device theft, storage mining and cryptographic obsolescence require dedicated security controls and conformance/evaluation artifacts. No linkability result covers them.

required_report_dimensions: training/validation/test subject split digests and pair-handle disjointness
attacker implementation, configuration and fit data
validation-locked operating point and fixed-threshold test counts
top-1/top-k re-identification and worst-stratum outcomes when a retrieval task is defined
effective anonymity-set distribution with estimator and assumptions
payload size, p50/p95/p99 latency, peak memory and measured energy where production profiling is available
source/corpus/configuration/report digests and exact commit SHA

pilot_minimums.meaning: screening floor only; not sufficient evidence and not an automatic pass

statistical_claim_ceiling.low_fpr: Select thresholds only on a disjoint validation cohort. Report resolution (1 / number of test negatives). Zero observed false positives is inconclusive for rare-event risk.
statistical_claim_ceiling.dependence: Pairs sharing subjects are correlated; pair-level binomial intervals alone are optimistic. Use subject- or cluster-aware uncertainty and state all assumptions.
statistical_claim_ceiling.prevalence: Report deployment or scenario prevalence explicitly. ROC-AUC is prevalence-insensitive and cannot alone communicate operational precision/false-alarm burden.
statistical_claim_ceiling.no_universal_score: No scalar aggregate may conceal a successful attacker, failed utility task, untested channel, or inapplicable format.

qualification_rule: Design mapping, synthetic smoke success, real-artifact attack evidence, utility evidence, and official protocol conformance are separate evidence levels. Release qualification requires every applicable gate and exact-head receipts; a queued, skipped, stale, or synthetic-only run is not a privacy pass.
claim_ceiling: This matrix is a research coverage proposal, not evidence of complete threat coverage, mitigation efficacy, standard conformance, a differential-privacy guarantee, or SOTA superiority.
